why: Both move essentially the same traffic with the same two policy unlocks (drop seed, map retired snapshots), and both verify live, so the decision turns on the system-level judgment and on honesty about what did not move. B reads this product correctly — aider is the majority of the spend and is genuinely unroutable on the installed LiteLLM, the novelty loop is the high-volume cheap-task hot spot, the n=5 ensemble must not be silently shrunk — whereas A claims the aider traffic routed on a hook B shows is inert, and its improvement set stays inside the Router-policy file rather than questioning which calls should exist.
A_best: Rigorous, controlled measurement (POLICY=off control runs, cache write/read token breakdowns, short-prompt safety, explicit 'unmeasured' labels), and it folded the pre-existing anthropic>=1.13 temperature break into the migration itself, so the shipped branch's default --model path actually runs and routes; its proposal to port the Claude path onto /v1/responses is the single most expert Router insight in either report, since that is what would give the default traffic fallbacks, provider_timeout and cache keys at all.
B_best: The system-level read is product-specific and ranked well: aider (the biggest token consumer and longest contexts) is correctly diagnosed as unroutable on LiteLLM 1.81.10 with a concrete shim scoped as rework rather than half-built; the novelty check — up to 500 calls per run of a mechanical read-and-decide task — is proposed onto a $0.20/1M Flex-eligible model with the quality risk stated honestly; plus a cross-vendor fallback chain and a per-key spend cap for an unattended workload that can run through a weekend.
A_worst: It asserts aider's LiteLLM traffic now routes via install_litellm(), which B documents as inert on the installed LiteLLM (no client_session anywhere in 1.81.10) — and even on A's own account the default aider model is Claude, which it admits is untouched, so the headline claim of moving the pipeline's largest spend is at best unsupported; it also contradicts itself on the n=5 ensemble (listed as 'now: router' in calls, as staying on the provider in the summary), dismisses Flex instead of asking which models should change to get it, and proposes no spend cap and no cheaper model for the highest-call-count loop.
B_worst: The anthropic temperature fix lives only on an improvement branch, so the shipped migration branch's default --model path still raises TypeError before any request — the thing B calls 'ranked first' is not in the migration it asks you to merge; measurements are also thinner (no control-run discipline), and having correctly noted that /v1/messages supports no Router policy fields, it never proposes porting the Claude path to Responses to fix that.
